kept.excerpt: Schwarber has been his typical big-swinging self for the Phillies, with the 5-foot-11 designated hitter batting .238, to go along with a league-leading 44 home runs, a top-10 94 RBIs and .869 OPS, good enough for 12th in the league.
kept.publisher: Athlon Sports via Yahoo Sports — Will Chesanek
kept.relevance: Provides a cutoff-day report of Schwarber's home-run lead and batting performance.

kept.excerpt: Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 42nd homer to match the Cubs record for a left-handed batter and finished with four hits and four RBIs to power Chicago past the Atlanta Braves 7-3 on Monday night. Crow-Armstrong’s two-run shot to right in the sixth inning off AJ Smith-Shawver pulled him even with Hall of Famer Billy Williams’ mark from 1970. Chicago has won three of four and moved one-half game ahead of idle Philadelphia for the top NL wild card.
kept.publisher: Associated Press via Daily Herald — Matt Carlson
kept.relevance: Establishes Crow-Armstrong's 42 home runs on the cutoff date, two behind Schwarber's reported 44, and confirms Philadelphia was idle that day.

kept.excerpt: Those All-Star sluggers have seized the home run and RBI leads from Alvarez, although the Houston Astros star still leads the American League with a .310 batting average entering play Monday, Sept. 14. Alvarez is just two homers behind Caminero's 40 and four RBI behind Alonso's 100, giving him a window to steal back the crowns by season's end. The article's AL home-run leaderboard, through games played September 13, lists Junior Caminero with 40, Yordan Alvarez and Ben Rice with 38 each, Pete Alonso with 35, and Kazuma Okamoto with 32.
kept.publisher: USA TODAY via AOL — Gabe Lacques
kept.relevance: Identifies the leading American League challengers and their deficits to Schwarber immediately before cutoff-day games.

kept.excerpt: Kyle Schwarber hit a grand slam for his majors-leading 44th home run, Trea Turner also homered and the Philadelphia Phillies overcame two deficits to beat the Houston Astros 11-7 on Wednesday night. Schwarber connected on a 3-2 sweeper from reliever A.J. Blubaugh to cap a six-run sixth inning. It was Schwarber’s 10th career grand slam and his fourth home run in the last five games.
kept.publisher: Associated Press via ABC News — Anthony Sanfilippo
kept.relevance: Corroborates Schwarber's 44-homer total and documents his recent burst of four home runs in five games.

kept.excerpt: Crow-Armstrong became the first Cub with a 40-plus home run season since Derrek Lee in 2005.
kept.relevance: Provides official MLB context for a principal challenger's power production entering the final weeks.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-09-14, inclusive; September 14 evening reporting is included. Every retained item has an explicit publication date visible in web_search results. Only dated reporting on or before the cutoff was used; later developments, undated live season totals, betting pages, odds, and prediction-market material were excluded. Excerpts are factual source text or faithful factual summaries. Full-page verification was limited: web_fetch failed because multiple fetch providers were registered, and the requested agent-reach web read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so the pack relies on dated article text exposed by web_search. The September 14 American League leaderboard explicitly covers games through September 13 and should not be treated as an end-of-September-14 leaderboard. A complete official cutoff-day MLB leaderboard and contemporaneous slugging-percentage tiebreak data were not verified.
